summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Fiserv’s CEO eyes monetization
articles.description: Takis Georgakopoulos is trying to reposition the company so it’s better able to sell its key payments and banking services.

articles.title: Klarna props up new Apple phones
articles.description: The buy now, pay later company will provide lease financing for a $2,000 phone to U.S. consumers coveting the latest Apple devices.

articles.title: The cost of friction: What 1,500 merchants told us about payments in 2026
articles.description: Payment expectations are changing merchant loyalty. Learn what platforms can do to reduce friction.

articles.title: Visa offers data to back onchain lending
articles.description: The card network aims to offer settlement and blockchain data so fintechs and card programs backed by stablecoins can better access onchain credit.

articles.title: PayPal CEO plans for a ‘fix’
articles.description: Can selling financial services to consumers, organizing the business into three units and pursuing acquisitions repair the digital payments pioneer?

articles.title: Trump pledges card fee cuts, again
articles.description: The president reiterated his support for policies to cut fees associated with credit cards, noting the charges are a burden for consumers.

articles.title: Circle buys Tazapay for $400M
articles.description: The stablecoin issuer will gain new payment rails and bank relationships via the Singapore-based cross-border payments firm.

articles.title: Zip explores an EWA play
articles.description: The buy now, pay later company may start a U.S. earned wage access service as an “income-smoothing” complement to its business.
